newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists split between up-neutral.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT - Dutch chartists split between up-neutral.

text.p: Some Dutch chartists are beginning to switch to a neutral stance from an uptrend, while others maintain their bullish outlook for the coming week, but the overall idea is that the trend will be up in the medium and longer run.
"Our indicators are warning us for a short-term correction," ABN AMRO said, adding staying neutral would be the best strategy until the index has chosen a clear direction on the short term.
ABN AMRO said a down move could take the AEX to levels close to the 700 level without harming the medium uptrend.
ING Barings said that an eventual dip towards the lower side of the rising trend channel-- around 705-710 points -- should provide the next buying opportunity.

The AEX index, which opened a little lower on Monday, was 1.30 points higher at just over 730 points by late afternoon. It finished last Friday at 728.92, up around nine points on the previous Friday. The all-time high of 742.40 was set last week.

ING Barings - Recent downside violation of first support at 730 has slightly weakened the internal technicals of the AEX. Current charts, suggesting minor support at 722, do not rule out a correction towards the lower side of its 8-week rising trend channel around 705-710. Fast momentum is peaking, confirming a correction phase. However, slow momentum still looks very positive showing that the medium term uptrend (4-6 months) is still intact. Money flow indicators of the Amsterdam stock market are topping a bit, suggesting some selling pressure is kicking in.

As the medium term and long term charts of the AEX remain bullish, with initial targets of around 770, we advise a neutral position for the next few days. But an eventual dip towards the lower side of the rising trend channel around 705-710, should provide the next buying opportunity.

IRIS - The AEX tested support last Friday (on an intra-day basis) and seems to be resuming its uptrend. We expect at least a test of the resistance formed by the all-time high. If the AEX is able to take out this level a further rise can be expected. Technical indicators are confirming this bullish scenario.

ABN AMRO - The AEX has reached a short term consolidation period since the end of last week. Subsequently, our indicators are warning us for a short term correction. This down move can take the AEX to levels close to the 700-level without harming the medium term uptrend. There the index meets the bottom of its trend-channel which has been effective since the beginning of December. In case prices piece through this trendline, fair support is found at 686. However, we advise to focus on the 730-level before entering into short positions.

After a fast, spiky, corrective move we expect the AEX to resume its way up and to place a renewed attack on previous highs. In case this correction doesn't occur we advise to re-enter long positions above all-time high at 742.40.
Summarising the above, we state that staying neutral is the best strategy until the index has chosen a clear direction on the short term.

MEESPIERSON - We expect the market to move sideways this week in a trading range with support at 705-710 and resistance at 730-732 area. Due to the after-expiration period volatility is expected to stay high as well. The short uptrend is weakening due to worsening environmental circumstances. The US dollar versus the German mark broke the support at 1.68. The German bunds look a bit toppy as well.
